@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@ +

Four kyc routes act only for the signed-in subject (or a platform role on the two reads) — KS-2166

+
What to know. These routes now answer 403 FORBIDDEN / “Forbidden” to a signed-in caller who is not the user they act on: +
    +
  • GET /api/kyc/:id and GET /api/kyc/user/:userId: the subject, or SYSTEM_ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN (the shared isPlatformRole);
    • +
  • DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data and POST /api/kyc/initiate (the body’s userId): the subject only, no admin exception.
    • +
+ The caller is req.user.userId; ids compare after an ASCII-only case fold. A test or tool that calls these routes as someone other than the subject (or with no user) now gets 403 where it got 200 or 201. +
Red at develop: 61 of 83 new cells. With the change 83 of 83, and the whole kyc suite 173 of 173. 18 of 18 mutants killed. Five existing files changed their test principal only (0 assertion lines changed). +
+
Not measured here. A running stack; callers outside this repository; the four platform suites; Node 24; any deploy; the tree merged with PR 2211. +

@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@ +

. Four kyc routes now act only for the signed-in subject, or a platform role on the two reads (KS-2166)

+
What this changes. Four kyc routes took the user they act on from the path or the request body and never compared it with the signed-in caller, so any signed-in caller could read, list, erase or start another person’s identity verification: +
    +
  • GET /api/kyc/:id: now the subject (the record’s userId, after the lookup) or a platform role;
    • +
  • GET /api/kyc/user/:userId: now the subject or a platform role;
    • +
  • DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data: now the subject only (erasure is irreversible; the GDPR erasure arrives on the user.erased bus, not here);
    • +
  • POST /api/kyc/initiate: now the subject named by the body’s userId only (the consent it records is the subject’s own).
    • +
+ A refusal is 403 { success: false, error: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', message: 'Forbidden' } }, the 403 the spec already declared on all four. On the list, DELETE and initiate it comes before any statement (initiate: after the body parse, so an invalid body is still 400). On GET /:id it follows the lookup, so a missing record is still 404 and a 403 confirms that a (service-minted v4 UUID) id exists: ruled acceptable. +
Who the caller is: req.user.userId from the verified token, never sub or an x-user-* header. One helper, callerMayActOn, decides for all four: both ids non-empty strings, equal after an ASCII-only case fold (A to Z lowered; a UUID’s hex is case-insensitive, and toLowerCase() would admit U+212A KELVIN SIGN as k). A platform role is the shared isPlatformRole (SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN); ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN, connector, an array role, no role and no principal are refused. +
One new test file (ks2166-kyc-routes-refuse-a-caller-who-is-not-the-subject.test.ts, 83 cells). Five existing files change their test principal only, with no assertion changed (a counted diff of expect( lines reads 0): ks849-mock-timer-stale-write (its helper now initiates as the subject it creates; every other call stays the admin principal) and four ks1868-* files (save-consent, save-verification, save-image-attestation, get-verifications-by-user), whose stand-in set no user and now signs in as the subject the file uses. +
+

.1 What proves it

+
Red at develop, green after, every mutant killed. Red-first with the unchanged index.ts (develop ed5b86ea20ae): 61 of the 83 new cells red, every one of them named RED; the 22 controls (the subject served unchanged, a platform role reading, the 400, the 404, the routing cell) green. +
With the change, the new file 83 of 83. The whole kyc suite before the principal repairs: 158 of 173, the 15 reds exactly ks849 S1 to S3 and the four ks1868 files (3 each). After them: 17 files / 173 of 173 (the cut’s baseline was 16 files / 90 of 90). +
Mutants: 18 of 18 killed, each a one-replacement tamper of index.ts restored by sha256: the check removed per route (4); the compare inverted; the fold removed; the fold widened to toLowerCase(); each conjunct of the platform exception and of the owner compare dropped separately (4); the exception put on DELETE, on initiate, or widened to ORG_ADMIN; the DELETE check moved after the erase (killed by the zero-DELETE assertion alone: the status still read 403); the initiate row keyed by the caller instead of the body; the initiate check moved after the consent check; GET /:id refusing before the lookup. A planted failing cell turned the run red (rc 1) and was restored by blob hash. +
tsc --noEmit on the service rc 0; tsc over the service source plus its 17 test files (a scratch config) rc 0. +
+

.2 Not covered

+
Not measured here. A running stack, a real token through the gateway to kyc, Postgres, the user.erased bus path, Node 24, a container build, any caller outside this repository (a non-subject caller now gets 403 where it got 200), the four platform suites, and the suite on a tree merged with PR 2211 (its ks1931 cells call the list and DELETE with no user: C1 and C2 turn red, R1 and R2 pass for the wrong reason until their principal is the subject). +
